svg.title: Track strand identity across two replication rounds
svg.desc: A duplex with two heavy original strands is replicated in light material. After one round, two duplexes each contain one heavy original strand and one light new strand. After two rounds, four duplexes include two hybrid and two all-light duplexes, with both original heavy strands conserved across the population. A colour legend explicitly distinguishes original heavy from light-synthesized strands. Under semiconservative assumptions density classes are intermediate after one round and intermediate plus light after two. Conservative replication predicts separate heavy and light after one round; an intermediate first round alone does not exclude all dispersive models. The drawing is a model of molecular provenance, not an experimental tube, band photo or measured intensity.

g.text: Track strand identity across two replication rounds
Strand colours identify material origin; density is an independent measurement.
After one round in light medium
After two rounds: 2 hybrid duplexes + 2 light duplexes
Semiconservative: every daughter duplex receives one template strand and one new strand.
Density predictions: round 1 → one intermediate class; round 2 → intermediate and light classes.
Conservative model predicts separate heavy and light classes after round 1.
Dispersive models can also give an intermediate first round; later patterns help distinguish them.
These are molecule/model predictions, not a reproduced experimental tube or measured band intensity.
